title: Spell Levels and Magnitudes
heading: Levels
summary: Defines a spell's level as its base level from the guideline plus adjustments for Range, Duration, Target and size, and explains magnitudes (level divided by five, rounded up), which also give the vis cost of a ritual.
quotes: The magnitude of a spell is equal to one fifth of its level, rounded up.
the number of pawns of vis needed to cast a ritual spell
SPELL MAGNITUDE: Level/5 (rounded up)

title: The Central Rule of Spell Design
heading: The Central Rule
summary: The troupe may always override the guideline system and set a higher or lower level for an odd combination of Range, Duration, Target and effect; storyguides should not let the system force things past common sense.
quotes: The troupe may always intervene and declare that a certain combination of Range, Duration, Target, and effect warrants a higher or lower level than that described by the guidelines and the system below.

title: Level Guidelines
heading: Level Guidelines
summary: Explains that the guidelines give the lowest level at which a Ritual, Formulaic or Spontaneous spell can produce an effect, using the lowest Range, Duration and Target as the baseline.
quotes: the range of the spell is Personal, the duration is Momentary, and the target is Individual.

title: Ranges, Durations, Targets (overview)
heading: Ranges, Durations, Targets
summary: Introduces the three spell parameters and their ordering by difficulty. Spontaneous spells must use the standard categories, while Formulaic and Ritual spells may be invented with non-standard ones at troupe discretion.
quotes: The Range governs how far the target can be from the magus, the Duration determines how long the target will be affected, and the Target describes what the spell can affect.

title: Changing Ranges, Durations and Targets
heading: Changing Ranges, Durations, and Targets
summary: Shows how to calculate a spell's level when its Range, Duration or Target is raised or lowered from the base, a magnitude per step, with a special rule that below level five a magnitude is a single level. Includes a worked example.
quotes: add one magnitude (five levels) to the level of the spell for every step by which the parameter is raised
Below level 5, adding a magnitude only adds one level, and subtracting a magnitude only subtracts one level.

title: Range, Duration and Target Table
heading: Ranges, Durations, and Targets
summary: Table ranking every Range, Duration, Object, Container and Sense target by the additional magnitudes it adds to a guideline.

title: Spell Ranges
heading: Ranges
summary: Describes each Range (Personal, Touch, Eye, Voice, Sight, Arcane Connection): how distance to the nearest part of the target is measured, how far a voice carries, what eye contact requires, and how continuing spells behave if the caster moves away.
quotes: The range of a spell is the distance to the nearest part of the target of the spell.
Typically, firm words carry about 15 paces, while quiet words are audible within 5 paces and a shout carries about 50.

title: Spell Durations
heading: Durations
summary: Describes each Duration (Momentary, Concentration, Diameter, Sun, Ring, Moon, Year), what happens to momentary effects under longer durations, recasting a spell to keep it continuous, and the rules for drawing a Ring.
quotes: In the absence of distractions, assume that a magus can concentrate for fifteen minutes per point of Concentration ability.
A spell with this duration must be ritual.
related: ArM5 p.215 Hermetic Magic chapter, concentration rules

title: Spell Targets
heading: Target
summary: Describes the object, container and sense Targets (Individual, Circle, Part, Group, Room, Structure, Boundary), what each can affect, and which require Ritual casting.
quotes: There are three types of target: objects, containers, and senses.
A spell with this target must be a Ritual.

title: Magical Senses
heading: Magical Senses
summary: Intellego spells can grant a magical sense (Taste, Touch, Smell, Hearing, Vision) as a Target; the information is limited like the mundane sense, must penetrate Magic Resistance, and one spell grants only one sense.
quotes: A single spell grants a single magical sense.

title: Magical Wards
heading: Magical Wards
summary: Rego wards protect the thing targeted from things of a Form; Circle wards bar crossing in both directions, are usually Ring Duration, and must Penetrate and equal or beat the Might of what they hold off.
quotes: because a ward with these parameters wards against creatures with a Might equal to or less than its level

title: Magical Craft (Creo and Rego)
heading: Magical Craft
summary: Rules for making natural and artificial things with magic: Creo creates natural objects directly, Rego rearranges materials like a craftsman, and a Finesse roll sets details and quality with Ease Factors based on mundane craft.
quotes: REGO CRAFT MAGIC ROLL: Perception + Finesse
CREO CRAFT MAGIC ROLL: Intelligence + Finesse
BASE EASE FACTOR: Highest Ease Factor for a Mundane Craftsman + 3

title: Ease Factors for Creating and Crafting Objects
heading: Ease Factors for Creating and Crafting Objects
summary: Table of crafting task difficulty with Ease Factors (including the adjustment for magic) from Trivial to Almost Impossible, with examples, for use with the Finesse craft rolls.

title: Summoning Spirits
heading: Summoning Spirits
summary: Hermetic magic can bring a spirit instantly to the caster without granting control. A Formulaic or Spontaneous spell suffices for a spirit in Mythic Europe, but a spirit in another realm needs a Ritual.
quotes: Summoning spells are normally cast at Arcane Connection range, making them quite high level.

title: Static and Dynamic Container Targets
heading: Static and Dynamic Targets
summary: Spells with container Targets either affect what is inside at the moment of casting (static) or whatever is inside throughout the duration (dynamic); this is fixed when the spell is designed and gives two different spells.
quotes: This is the way that spells with object Targets work, and can be referred to as a static target
This can be referred to as a dynamic target, because the things that are targeted by the spell can change over the duration.

title: Being Inside a Container
heading: Being Inside a Container
summary: Uses an intuitive definition of what counts as inside a Circle, Room, Structure or Boundary, with examples, and lets the troupe be more precise if needed.

title: Persistence of Containers
heading: Persistence of Containers
summary: Explains when a container target still exists for a spell (same container, moved, resized, rebuilt) and why Circles and bare-marker Boundaries are vulnerable to being broken or altered.

title: Targets and Sizes
heading: Targets and Sizes
summary: Target types depend on kind of thing not size, but the size of the target affects spell level in every Form except Intellego and Circle targets: each magnitude added multiplies the allowed mass or volume. Gives the base Part, Group, Room, Structure and Boundary sizes, and how to adjust for enlarging or shrinking.
quotes: Adding one magnitude (five levels) to the spell multiplies the maximum size of its target by ten.
A base Room is large enough to fit a hundred standard Individuals with some squashing.
Mass of ten standard Individuals

title: Targets and Creo
heading: Targets and Creo
summary: A Creo spell's Target is the thing created, always Individual or Group; creating a part of something is healing or Muto, and filling a room needs a Group target with a size modifier.
quotes: The target of a Creo spell that actually creates something is the thing created.

title: Volumes and Targets
heading: Volumes and Targets
summary: Reference list of volumes in tenfold steps, each equal to one magnitude of size, matched to base Individuals for several Forms and to the Material and Size table.
related: ArM5 p.255 Material and Size table

title: Ritual Spells
heading: Ritual Spells
summary: Lists what only Ritual spells can do or must be Ritual: Year Duration, Boundary Target, levels above the Formulaic limit, lasting Momentary Creo creations, and effects the troupe judges too spectacular. Rituals have a minimum level and cannot be replicated spontaneously.
quotes: Ritual spells are always at least level 20, even if the level calculation would make them lower.
Formulaic and Spontaneous spells may not have a level greater than 50.
It is never possible to replicate the effects of a Ritual spell with Spontaneous magic, even when casting Ceremonially.

title: Requisites
heading: Requisites
summary: Explains requisite Arts: those needed for the effect add no levels, those that add an effect add at least a magnitude. A requisite limits the casting score to the lower of it and the primary Art, and requisites never change Magic Resistance or vis matching.
quotes: REQUISITE NECESSARY FOR SPELL'S EFFECT: +0 magnitudes
REQUISITE ENHANCES SPELL'S EFFECT: +1 magnitude or more
ADDED EFFECT IS PURELY COSMETIC: No requisite

title: Casting Requisites
heading: Casting Requisites
summary: Casting requisites are chosen at casting time rather than listed with the spell; the lowest Technique and Form among the primary and chosen requisite Arts is used for the Casting Total.

title: Spontaneous Requisites
heading: Spontaneous Requisites
summary: Requisites limit the Arts of Spontaneous spells in the same way as Formulaic ones.

title: How to Read a Spell (Technique and Form)
heading: Spell Format
summary: Explains how spells are presented (grouped by Form then Technique), that guideline Range, Duration and Target default to Personal, Momentary and Individual unless noted, and the two-letter abbreviation style such as CrIg 15.
quotes: If the guideline does not specify a Range, Duration, or Target, they are Personal, Momentary, and Individual.

title: General Level Spells
heading: Level
summary: General (Gen) spells can be learned at any level; the level at which you know one is where you learned or invented it, it cannot be used above or below that level, and each level is a different spell.
quotes: General level spells are open-ended only in the sense that they may be learned at any level.

title: Spell Design Line
heading: Design
summary: Describes the parenthetical calculation at the end of each spell: base level in levels plus modifications in magnitudes, with the reminder that a magnitude is one level up to level five.

title: Spell Damage
heading: Spell Damage
summary: Spell damage written as +X means a stress die plus X, rolled anew each casting, which the target resists with Soak Total plus a stress die.
quotes: This is an abbreviation for stress die + X.
The target resists this damage with their Soak Total + stress die.
related: ArM5 Combat chapter, damage and Soak

title: The Wizard's Sigil
heading: The Wizard's Sigil
summary: A magus's personal quirk that shows up in the spells they invent and identifies the caster; it does not usually change effectiveness, and learned spells still carry your own sigil.
quotes: it is always your sigil that manifests in your spells.
related: ArM5 p.224 Hermetic Magic chapter, sigils

title: Animal: How It Works
heading: Animal Spells
summary: What Animal magic covers and the boundary with Mentem and Corpus: creatures with Cunning are affected by Animal in the mind, those with Intelligence need Mentem. Covers shapechangers, Bjornaer in animal form, animal parts on humans, and the base Individual.
quotes: If the creature has Intelligence, a Mentem spell must be used. If it has Cunning, an Animal spell must be used.
A basic Individual for Animal is an animal of about the same size as a pony, Size +1 or lower.

title: Aquam: How It Works
heading: Aquam Spells
summary: What Aquam affects (water and other liquids, but not liquids that are part of a body without special design), how target categories apply to bodies of liquid, and base Individual sizes for water, natural, processed and corrosive liquids and poisons.
quotes: A base Individual for Aquam is a pool of water about five paces (fifteen feet) across, and two paces deep at the center.

title: Auram: How It Works
heading: Auram Spells
summary: Auram covers air and most weather; explains how Individual and Group apply to weather phenomena and gives the base Individual as a phenomenon affecting a Boundary-sized area.
quotes: A base Individual for Auram is a weather phenomenon that affects the area within a standard Boundary

title: Corpus: How It Works
heading: Corpus Spells
summary: Corpus affects human and humanlike bodies, including many faeries, and the base Individual is an adult human.
quotes: A base Individual for Corpus is an adult human being, up to Size +1.

title: Herbam: How It Works
heading: Herbam Spells
summary: Herbam covers living and dead plants and plant matter including wood, and its base Individual is a plant about a pace in each direction.
quotes: A base Individual for Herbam is a plant roughly one pace in each direction.

title: Ignem: How It Works
heading: Ignem Spells
summary: Ignem covers fire, light and heat (including cold as absence of heat); warns that botches should be deadly, and gives the base Individual as a large campfire.
quotes: The base Individual for Ignem is a large campfire or the fire in the hearth of a great hall.

title: Imaginem: How It Works
heading: Imaginem Spells
summary: Imaginem affects images and sensations rather than light or minds: how beasts, demons, faeries and the Church react to illusions, and a Perception + Finesse stress roll with Ease Factors to mimic specific objects or people.
quotes: It is more difficult to mimic a specific object or person using an Imaginem spell than it is to mimic a general image, and requires a Perception + Finesse stress roll.

For mimicking people, a roll against an Ease Factor of 6 lets you fool acquaintances of the person, an Ease Factor of 9 lets you fool friends, and an Ease Factor of 12 lets you fool close friends and relatives.

title: Mentem: How It Works
heading: Mentem Spells
summary: Mentem governs intelligent minds, thoughts, emotions, memories and the mental Characteristics; beasts need Animal magic. Minds have no size so size modifiers do not apply to Individual targets, but Groups and containers scale as normal.
quotes: Minds do not have a size, so size modifiers do not apply to Mentem effects with Individual targets.

title: Terram: How It Works
heading: Terram Spells
summary: Terram covers earth, stone, clay, metal, glass and many inanimate objects. It lists materials in order of difficulty and gives base Individual sizes that depend on the material.
quotes: it is harder to affect certain materials: Here, in increasing order of difficulty, are the materials Terram spells affect: earth (sand, dirt, mud), clay, stone, glass, metal, gemstones.

title: Vim: How It Works
heading: Vim Spells
summary: How Vim magic works: it acts on spells, magical effects, spirits and demons, most Vim spells are General level and their guidelines relate the Vim spell's level to the level of the target, with modified Range or Target costing power. Spells and effects have no size.
quotes: Most Vim spells are of General level, because the magic that Vim spells affect varies widely in power.

title: Creo Animal Notes
heading: Creo Animal Guidelines
summary: Notes on creating animals and animal products: treated and processed products cost extra magnitudes, created animals just act naturally unless a Rego requisite is added, and Personal range is rarely usable.
quotes: Most Animal spells cannot be used with Personal range, so the level of a spell must be higher than the guidelines given.

title: Perdo Animal Notes
heading: Perdo Animal Guidelines
summary: Perdo Animal causes damage directly, so there is normally no Soak against it and only Magic Resistance defends.
quotes: There is normally no Soak against Perdo Animal

title: Creo Aquam Notes
heading: Creo Aquam Guidelines
summary: Created water only quenches thirst temporarily; unnatural liquids cost extra magnitudes and need Muto requisites; poisons created have a base Ease Factor that rises with each magnitude.
quotes: Poisons created at the guideline level have an Ease Factor of 3. Each magnitude added to the level of the spell adds 3 to the Ease Factor.

title: Muto Aquam Notes
heading: Muto Aquam Guidelines
summary: Liquids inside a body can only be transformed by a spell designed for it with a Corpus or Animal requisite; poisons made by Muto use the same Ease Factor scaling as Creo Aquam.
quotes: Poisons created at the guideline level have an Ease Factor of 3. For every magnitude added to the spell, add three to the Ease Factor.

title: Rego Aquam Notes
heading: Rego Aquam Guidelines
summary: Rego Aquam can turn water to ice or steam; slightly or very unnatural controlled movement costs extra magnitudes.
quotes: Rego Aquam can change water into ice or steam, because these are both states that water can have naturally.

title: Creo Auram Notes
heading: Creo Auram Guidelines
summary: Weather is normally created at Sight range because it begins in the upper air; ground-level weather is unnatural and its extra cost cancels the saving from shorter range.
quotes: Weather phenomena are normally created at Sight range.

title: Rego Auram Notes
heading: Rego Auram Guidelines
summary: Rego Auram controls existing weather, including starting and stopping rain, but cannot create a breeze; precise or powerful control raises the magnitude.
quotes: It is not possible to create a breeze with Rego Auram, but it is possible to direct the course of a storm.

title: Creo Corpus Healing Rules
heading: Creo Corpus Guidelines
summary: Rules for healing with magic: only a Momentary Duration Ritual heals permanently, otherwise the healing is suspended and wounds return; healing a wound level also heals lesser ones; wounds and diseases need separate spells; Fatigue cannot be restored; physical Characteristics can be improved.
quotes: a healing spell cast other than as a Momentary Duration Ritual actually suspends the healing process so that, upon the spell's expiration, wounds are as fresh as they were when the spell was cast.
No Hermetic spell can restore Fatigue levels.
a spell to heal wounds cannot cure diseases, no matter how high its level, and vice versa.

title: Muto Corpus Shapechanging Rules
heading: Muto Corpus Guidelines
summary: Rules for transforming people: the original form leaves traces, long stays in animal form change behaviour, the mind and knowledge stay intact, magi can cast in animal form with the no-hands-or-voice penalty, worn items need casting requisites, and foci allow the target to change back.
quotes: Magi can cast spells while in animal form, but they suffer the normal –15 penalty for casting without hands or voice.
Muto Corpus spells cannot alter a person's mind, so they leave the transformed person's intelligence and knowledge intact.

title: Perdo Corpus Notes
heading: Perdo Corpus Guidelines
summary: Perdo Corpus harm is often permanent unless repaired by other magic; diseases inflicted by magic have a base Ease Factor that rises with each magnitude and cannot be reduced by lowering level.
quotes: Diseases caused by magic have a base Ease Factor of 6. For every magnitude by which the spell level increases, the Ease Factor increases by 1.

title: Rego Corpus Notes
heading: Rego Corpus Guidelines
summary: Rego Corpus can perform surgery; detailed surgical rules are in another book.
quotes: Rego Corpus can be used to perform surgery.

title: Creo Herbam Notes
heading: Creo Herbam Guidelines
summary: Created food is nutritious only if the spell is a Ritual; plants can be created living or dead; treated and processed plant products cost extra magnitudes; one spell creates one type of plant product.
quotes: Any food created is nutritious only if the creation is a Ritual.

title: Muto Ignem Notes
heading: Muto Ignem Guidelines
summary: More intense fires are harder to change: spell level rises with the fire's damage above a threshold.
quotes: For every five points by which the fire's damage exceeds +5, add one magnitude to the level of the spell.

title: Perdo Ignem Notes
heading: Perdo Ignem Guidelines
summary: More intense fires are harder to destroy: spell level rises with the fire's damage above a threshold; botches may create fire or freeze the caster.
quotes: For every five points by which the fire's damage exceeds +5, add one magnitude to the level of the spell.

title: Rego Ignem Notes
heading: Rego Ignem Guidelines
summary: More intense fires are harder to control, with a magnitude added for each step of fire damage above a threshold; Rego Ignem also controls heat and light.
quotes: Rego Ignem spells can control heat or light as well as fire.

title: Creo Imaginem Notes
heading: Creo Imaginem Guidelines
summary: Creo Imaginem makes only images, not the things themselves (an image bucket holds no water); extra complexity, movement, intelligible speech or intricacy add magnitudes.
quotes: Creo Imaginem spells only create the images of things, not the things themselves.

title: Intellego Imaginem Notes
heading: Intellego Imaginem Guidelines
summary: Intellego Imaginem detects real images at a distance; it needs light or sound at the place observed, and each extra sense perceived adds a magnitude.
quotes: each additional sense you wish to perceive increases the level of the spell by one magnitude

title: Muto Imaginem Notes
heading: Muto Imaginem Guidelines
summary: Muto Imaginem alters existing images and persists without concentration; mimicking a specific voice or face needs familiarity and acquaintances may see through it; Imaginem cannot overcome the Gift.
quotes: Muto Imaginem, or indeed other Imaginem magic, cannot overcome the effects of The Gift, although it might offset them a little.

title: Perdo Imaginem Notes
heading: Perdo Imaginem Guidelines
summary: Perdo Imaginem dulls the senses an object affects (including invisibility); destroying changing images costs more, Momentary duration only makes an object flicker, shadows are Ignem not Imaginem, and mirror images follow the changed species.
quotes: Destroying something's shadow is thus Creo Ignem, or possibly Rego Ignem, not Perdo Imaginem.

title: Rego Imaginem Notes
heading: Rego Imaginem Guidelines
summary: Rego Imaginem displaces where an image appears to be; changing images and images that change with the object cost extra magnitudes, as does each additional sense.
quotes: Add one level of magnitude to the guidelines for each additional sense to be affected.

title: Intellego Mentem Notes
heading: Intellego Mentem Guidelines
summary: A Momentary Intellego Mentem spell can answer a single question, however complex the feeling, but not why; writing is not Mentem (it is Animal and Herbam or Terram), so translation needs a reader.
quotes: In general, a momentary Mentem spell can answer a single question, although it is not necessary that the answer be expressible in a brief form.

title: Muto Mentem Notes
heading: Muto Mentem Guidelines
summary: Muto Mentem covers changed memories, unnatural thoughts and emotions, and making a mind physical. Also explains how to grant a magical sense to many people at once, using Muto Mentem with Intellego and Form requisites.
quotes: granting a magical sense to multiple people is a function of Muto Mentem.

title: Perdo Mentem Notes
heading: Perdo Mentem Guidelines
summary: Destroyed emotions return naturally so need a continuing Duration; destroyed memories stay gone with Momentary Duration unless a continuing spell prevents relearning.
quotes: Emotions naturally reappear in a person, so spells that destroy them must have a continuing duration to ensure that they do not come back.

title: Creo Terram Notes
heading: Creo Terram Guidelines
summary: Creating earth in an elaborate shape, or with an unnatural property and a Muto requisite, costs an extra magnitude; botches can entomb the caster.
quotes: Creating earth in an elaborate shape or, with a Muto requisite, with some unnatural property is one level of magnitude higher than the listed guidelines.

title: Muto Terram Notes
heading: Muto Terram Guidelines
summary: Guidelines assume dirt; changing to or from stone or glass, or metal or gemstone, adds magnitudes once, and the amount changed is limited by the base Individual at each end.
quotes: To change to or from stone or glass, add one level of magnitude. To change to or from metal or gemstone, add two levels of magnitude.

title: Perdo Terram Notes
heading: Perdo Terram Guidelines
summary: Guidelines assume dirt; destroying stone or glass adds a magnitude and metal or gemstone adds more; botches can destroy the ground under the caster or metal they hold.
quotes: To destroy stone or glass, add one magnitude. To destroy metal or gemstone, add two magnitudes.

title: Rego Terram Notes
heading: Rego Terram Guidelines
summary: Guidelines assume dirt; controlling stone or glass adds a magnitude and metal or gemstones add two, except when simply moving an item, and very precise manipulation costs more.
quotes: Add one magnitude to control stone or glass, and two for metal or gemstones, unless the item is simply being moved from one place to another

title: Intellego Vim: Detecting Magic and Spell Residues
heading: Intellego Vim Guidelines
summary: How magic detection works: the base level gives rough strength within a magnitude, extra magnitudes reveal realm, Arts, and details; items need a season in the lab to investigate; residues of spells halve and then decay over time; creatures and raw vis are detected by dedicated spells.
quotes: Investigation requires that you spend at least one season in the laboratory to discover what magic an enchanted item contains
As soon as the magic finishes, the magnitude halves.
A 'negative magnitude' of 10 indicates that the residue has disappeared completely, and no longer exists to be detected.

title: Muto Vim: Changing Other Spells
heading: Muto Vim Guidelines
summary: Rules for meta-magic that alters other Hermetic spells: not usable on Spontaneous spells, needs an Intelligence + Concentration roll when you cast both, timing and Penetration against another magus' spell, Duration at least as long as the target casting, and Ritual requirements.
quotes: you must make an Intelligence + Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of 9 if you are casting both spells
It is not possible, for reasons that Hermetic theorists do not well understand, to use Muto Vim to affect another spell after it has been cast.

title: Muto Vim Spells and Enchanted Devices
heading: Muto Vim Spells & Enchanted Devices
summary: When a Muto Vim effect may be put into a magic item, and how to use or counter one against a device's effect: cooperation and timing, fast casting, beating Penetration, and identifying the Form.
quotes: The caster must succeed with an Intelligence + Concentration roll against an Ease Factor of 9.
related: ArM5 p.217 Determining Form of Magical Effect

title: Aegis of the Hearth
heading: Aegis of the Hearth
summary: The covenant's Ritual protection that works like a Parma Magica over a boundary: bars supernatural creatures with Might below its level, forces foreign effects to Penetrate it, weakens foreign castings inside, and defines natives and invitations.
quotes: No foreign supernatural creature with Might, of any type, can cross the boundary of the Aegis unless its Might exceeds the level of the Aegis.
must Penetrate a Magic Resistance equal to the level of the Aegis of the Hearth to take effect
must subtract half the level of the Aegis from any Casting Total or equivalent

title: Wizard's Communion (Group Casting)
heading: Wizard's Communion
summary: Lets several magi pool power to cast one spell: limits on participants, the combined level needed, the reduced target number for the caster, extra botch dice per participant, and shared Warping on a botch.
quotes: Only one extra magus may join the Communion for each 5 levels of the specified spell being cast.
the target number for the spellcasting roll is the spell's level divided by the number of magi participating in the Communion
